transcript.statement: Sustainability is crucial for the Autonomous Driving System. GRN-01 ensures energy consumption is minimized, while GRN-02 promotes renewable energy usage, reducing the carbon footprint. GRN-03 focuses on lifecycle assessments, ensuring resource impact is considered. GRN-04 emphasizes energy recovery during braking, enhancing efficiency. GRN-05 aims for real-time emission monitoring, promoting accountability. GRN-06 prioritizes energy-efficient routing, and GRN-07 sets protocols for minimizing energy use during failures. These requirements collectively support environmental objectives and enhance public trust in autonomous systems.

transcript.statement: Trustworthiness is paramount for the safety and acceptance of autonomous driving systems. TRU-01 ensures user data protection through encryption, while TRU-02 enforces role-based access control to limit permissions. TRU-03 guarantees auditability by logging access and modifications, essential for accountability. TRU-04 protects user identities through anonymization, and TRU-05 mandates regular security audits to identify vulnerabilities. TRU-06 secures remote updates to prevent malware, and TRU-07 informs users about data practices, fostering transparency. Together, these requirements safeguard user trust and comply with regulatory standards.

requirements.text: The system shall implement a multi-layer safety architecture including passive, active, and functional safety mechanisms to ensure collision protection and fail-safe operations.
The system shall execute a Minimal Risk Maneuver within 5 seconds upon detecting critical failures to safely pull over to a low-risk zone while ensuring speed and comfort.
The system shall continuously monitor Operational Design Domain compliance and issue a human takeover request when boundaries are approached.
The system shall minimize jerk to less than 0.5 m/s³ during normal operation while allowing for flexibility in emergency maneuvers.
The system shall satisfy curvature constraints ($kappa$) to prevent rollover during maneuvers at all speeds.
The system shall utilize iterative quadratic programming to handle non-convex obstacle constraints reliably within a response time of 100 milliseconds.
The system shall optimize path planning to achieve a reduction in average travel time while ensuring energy efficiency targets are met.
The system shall maintain a jerk value below 0.5 m/s³ during normal operation to enhance passenger comfort.
The system shall continuously monitor ODD compliance with a latency of no more than 100 milliseconds to ensure real-time responsiveness.
The system shall achieve at least 95% success rate in optimal speed profile generation during path planning.
The system shall implement end-to-end data encryption for all user data transmitted to protect privacy and ensure data integrity.
The system shall log all access and modifications to critical data for auditability purposes.
The system shall conduct regular security audits at least bi-annually to identify and mitigate potential vulnerabilities.
The system shall ensure compliance with the Apollo Pilot Safety Report and EM Motion Planner specifications at all operational times.
The system shall implement a multi-layer safety architecture that guarantees active monitoring and response to critical system failures.
The system shall document all safety and compliance-related decisions and changes for accountability and regulatory purposes.
